name: Vietnam

rates.label: standard
rates.appliesTo: 2-point cut under Resolutions 101/2023, 142/2024, 259/2024 and 204/2025 (Decrees 44, 72, 94, 204 and 174); lapses 31 December 2026 unless extended

rates.label: reduced
rates.appliesTo: essential goods and services (water, medical, education, public transport, and others)

rates.label: standardExcluded
rates.appliesTo: telecommunications, financial activities, banking, securities, insurance, real estate, metal products, most mining, and goods and services subject to special consumption tax — never received the 2-point cut

Hanoi Tax Department (General Department of Taxation): Resolution 204/2025/QH15 — 2-point VAT cut (10% to 8%) from 1 July 2025 to 31 December 2026
Allen & Gledhill: Vietnam reduces VAT rate to 8% from 1 July 2023 (Resolution 101/2023/QH15 and Decree 44/2023 — window 1 July to 31 December 2023, later extended through 2024)
VATCalc: 2026 global VAT, GST and sales tax rates table (secondary compilation; the authority's own rate pages were not reachable for this country in this session)

caveats: individualTaxYear is the calendar year, inferred from the country's annual assessment cycle (grade I); not confirmed on the authority's own pages in this pass.
companyYearEndDefault is a 31 December app default for new entities (grade I), not a statutory requirement; companies may choose other year ends under national law.

The statutory rates are 0%, 5% and 10%; the 8% rows record the temporary 2-point cuts on the 10% track: 1 February 2022 to 31 January 2023 (Res. 43/2022), lapsed 1 January to 30 June 2023, 1 July 2023 to 31 December 2024 (Res. 101/2023, extended by Decree 94/2023 and Res. 142/2024), 1 January to 30 June 2025 (Res. 259/2024) and 1 July 2025 to 31 December 2026 (Res. 204/2025). Extension into 2027 was still under review in November 2026, so the open 8% row may lapse on 31 December 2026.

Lower-bound rows - standard (2022-01-01), reduced (2022-01-01), standardExcluded (2022-01-01): the `from` date is the earliest a source confirms the rate applied, not necessarily its true start (in force at the start of the coverage window on 1 January 2022).
